clue.text: Scallywag affected by onset of school

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its beginning, so only the opening letter of school is used

parts.note: only its first letter is taken
camp means showily affected or mannered in style

explanation.surface: A young rascal picks up bad mannerisms as soon as term begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected' looks like a verb about the scallywag being changed by school, but it is the adjective, meaning mannered.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamp is a mischievous rogue or rascal, a close synonym for a scallywag.

clue.text: Divert second big dipper

parts.note: to switch something is to divert it onto another track or course
to back a proposal is to second it, to support it

explanation.surface: Someone redirects a fairground ride, with a stray second in the mix.
explanation.walkthrough: A big dipper is the British name for a roller coaster at a funfair.
explanation.definitionFit: A switchback is an older word for a roller coaster, named for its steep up-and-down track.

clue.text: Friar Tuck shows crafty conduct

indicators.note: the phrase Friar Tuck shows, that is displays within itself, the answer across its two words

parts.note: the answer runs from the end of Friar into the start of Tuck

explanation.surface: Robin Hood's jolly friar reveals a sly side to his behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Art can mean cunning or trickery, as in artful, so crafty conduct is a fair sense.

clue.text: In flat, garland a talented septet

indicators.note: the garland is placed in the flat, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat or apartment
a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers

explanation.surface: Seven gifted performers share a flat decorated with a garland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pleiades were the seven daughters of Atlas; a pleiad came to mean any group of seven brilliant people, such as the French poets of the Pléiade.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleiad is a group of seven illustrious or gifted people, named after the star cluster.

clue.text: Second drink brought by servant

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
a porter is a servant who carries luggage or keeps a door

explanation.surface: A second round of drinks is brought over by the hotel staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like a time or an ordinal; it is the noun for a person who backs another, as in a duel.
explanation.definitionFit: A second in a duel or boxing match is a backer, an assistant who stands behind the principal.

clue.text: Flags rise above NI football club

indicators.note: in a down answer the first part sits above the second

parts.note: to stand is to rise to one's feet
Ards FC is a football club in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Banners go up over a Northern Irish football ground.
explanation.walkthrough: NI is Northern Ireland; Ards is a club from Newtownards in County Down.
explanation.definitionFit: Standards are flags or banners, especially ones carried as an emblem of a monarch or regiment.

clue.text: Strike buffoon

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to hit with the fist
second meaning: ..., the clownish hook-nosed puppet of ... and Judy shows

explanation.walkthrough: Punch and Judy is a traditional British seaside puppet show in which Punch is the clown.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works both as a verb for a blow with the fist and as the name of the puppet-show clown.

clue.text: Dress material in orange I'd ordered

indicators.note: the letters of orange I'd are put into a new order

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone recalls ordering a dress fabric in orange.
explanation.definitionFit: Organdie is a fine, stiff, sheer cotton fabric used for dresses.

clue.text: Break a leg in tavern brawling after time? I fix breaks

indicators.note: the rest of the answer comes after the letter for time
the rearranged a leg goes inside the rearranged tavern
the letters of tavern are thrown about as in a brawl

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the letters of a leg are broken up and reordered

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bar fight leaves someone with a broken leg, and a bonesetter offers to help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break a leg' reads as the theatre good-luck phrase and 'fix breaks' as setting bones; here the breaks are holidays.

clue.text: Part of film is serious, according to report

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the answer is spelt as a word that sounds like it

parts.note: real in the sense of genuine and serious, as in a real problem

explanation.surface: A critic finds part of a film weighty, as reported.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a spool holding one section of a film, so a film is made up of several of them.

clue.text: One gets them in a Scottish town, right away mostly

indicators.note: one gets, or acquires, what follows, so the pieces are joined

the letter for right is taken away from the town's name

parts.note: Nairn is a town on the Moray Firth in the Scottish Highlands
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone receives things in a Scottish town, with the reference to right mostly gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right away' reads as 'at once' but is an instruction to remove R from Nairn; 'mostly', the definition, also looks like an instruction to drop a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In the main is an idiom meaning on the whole, for the most part.

clue.text: Grand party, of importance

parts.note: a rave is a large lively party with dance music

explanation.surface: A lavish party is a significant occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave means weighty and serious, a matter of importance.

clue.text: Blow hot and cold about work accepted by labourer before shift

indicators.note: the earlier pieces come before the word for shift
the labourer takes in the word for work, so it sits inside

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
op is short for opus, a musical work
to change is to shift or alter

explanation.surface: A worker takes on a job and then wavers about moving.
explanation.walkthrough: C is circa, Latin for about; OP is opus, a numbered work.
explanation.definitionFit: To chop and change is an idiom for keep switching plans, like blowing hot and cold.

clue.text: Told off with force, going to walk across ground

indicators.note: off here means amiss, so the letters of Told are rearranged

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

to ford a river is to walk across it at a shallow point

explanation.surface: A scolding delivered forcefully before someone sets off on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Told off' reads as scolded; 'ground' looks like land underfoot but means a football stadium. Old Trafford is Manchester United's home ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Trafford is a famous English football stadium, Manchester United's home, and so a ground.

clue.text: Gambler needs tokens — thirty, initially, in advance

parts.note: a better is one who bets
men are the pieces or counters used in board games such as draughts

indicators.note: only the first letter of thirty is used

parts.note: only its first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A punter needs thirty chips up front before playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In advance' looks like 'paid ahead'; only 'advance' is the definition, in its sense of progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Betterment is improvement, and an advance is likewise a step forward or improvement.

clue.text: Lad holding key for the trunk

indicators.note: the lad holds the key inside him

parts.note: a boy is a lad
D is a musical key

explanation.surface: A boy clutches the key to a storage chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' looks like a luggage chest that a key opens; it means the torso.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk is the torso, the main part of the body apart from the head and limbs.

clue.text: Go ape with flirt, wildly extravagant type

indicators.note: the letters are scattered wildly into a new order

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone goes crazy flirting, a reckless spendthrift at heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A profligate is a wastefully extravagant or dissolute person, a spendthrift.

explanation.walkthrough: St Petersburg suggests Russia, but there is also a St Petersburg in Florida, USA.

clue.text: The man left, in one particular place, an old family piece

parts.note: he refers to a man
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the letter for left is put in among the following letters

parts.note: a room is one particular space within a building

explanation.surface: A man departed, leaving an antique in a special spot.
explanation.definitionFit: An heirloom is a valued object handed down through generations of a family.

clue.text: Small retail outlet in block off second short flight

parts.note: to corner someone is to block their escape
a hop is a short flight, as in a short plane journey

explanation.surface: A little shop sits in a block next to a short flight of stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: A corner shop is the British name for a small local convenience store.
explanation.definitionFit: A corner shop is a small local store selling everyday goods, a minor retail outlet.

clue.text: Flog Ecstasy in club

indicators.note: the letter for Ecstasy goes in the club

parts.note: a bat is a club used in games such as cricket and baseball
E is slang for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: A dealer sells drugs at a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' reads as British slang for sell, and 'club' as a nightclub; here flog means whip and club is a bat.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog someone is to whip or thrash them, so to strike repeatedly.

clue.text: Burly jumper, say, in circus tent

parts.note: big means large and strongly built
a jumper (a sweater) is one kind of top

explanation.surface: A heavyset acrobat performs inside the circus marquee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' suggests a trapeze artist; in British English it is a sweater, an example of a top.
explanation.definitionFit: The big top is the main marquee of a travelling circus, where shows are staged.

clue.text: Political leader, one in church behind cardinal

indicators.note: the part with the church comes behind, after, the word for cardinal

parts.note: cardinal means chief or principal, as is first

indicators.note: one is put inside the church

parts.note: a minster is a large church, such as York Minster
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' looks like the churchman, matching 'church'; here it is the adjective for chief.
explanation.definitionFit: A First Minister heads the devolved governments of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Follow river into dock

explanation.surface: Someone tracks a river down to the docks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dock' looks like a harbour beside the river; it is the docked tail of an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail someone is to follow them closely, tracking their movements.

clue.text: Miss sleep after start of storm

indicators.note: the word for sleep comes after that first letter
only the opening letter of storm is used

parts.note: only its first letter is taken
kip is British slang for sleep

explanation.surface: Someone loses sleep once a storm begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip a class or meal is to miss it, deliberately leaving it out.

clue.text: Former capital of Kentucky, too awful

parts.note: KY is the US postal abbreviation for Kentucky

indicators.note: the letters of too are mangled into a new order

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A visitor complains that Kentucky's old state capital is dreadful too.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a capital of Kentucky; the definition is just 'Former capital', of Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: Kyoto was the imperial capital of Japan for over a thousand years before Tokyo.

clue.text: Grow up, bearing child at length to philosopher

indicators.note: the word for grow up carries the child and length within it

parts.note: to arise is to come up or rise
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A child grows up to become a long-winded thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the ancient Greek thinker, a pupil of Plato and tutor of Alexander the Great.

clue.text: Meal of duck cut short

the verb for jump stretches across the sea's name

parts.note: to leap is to jump
Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea
taken as written

clue.text: Found workshop

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to establish or set up

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to establish something firmly and an industrial site such as a factory.
